unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Who originally designed and implemented the C programming language at AT&T Bell Laboratories in 1972?
explanation: Dennis Ritchie created C in 1972 at Bell Labs to implement the Unix operating system, evolving it from Ken Thompson's B language.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Which stage of the C compilation pipeline handles directives beginning with the hash symbol (#)?
explanation: The C preprocessor runs before semantic compilation, expanding header includes (#include), macro substitutions (#define), and conditional compilation (#ifdef).

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What file extension is typically given to an intermediate object file produced after compiling C source code on Windows / DOS?
explanation: The compiler converts source code (.c) into machine code object files (.obj on Windows/DOS, .o on Linux) prior to linking.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: The Linker in a C programming toolchain is responsible for:

options.text: Combining compiled object modules with runtime C standard library routines into an executable file (.exe)

explanation: The Linker resolves cross-file function calls and links library functions (e.g., printf, scanf from libc) to create a standalone executable binary.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Every standard C program execution must begin with which function?
explanation: The runtime environment invokes main() as the predefined program entry point where CPU instruction execution begins.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Which of the following is an invalid identifier name in C?
explanation: In C, identifier names must begin with an alphabetic letter (a-z, A-Z) or an underscore (_); starting with a digit (e.g. 2nd_student) is a syntax error.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: How many reserved keywords exist in the standard ANSI C (C89/C90) specification?
explanation: ANSI C89 defines exactly 32 reserved keywords (auto, break, case, char, const, continue, default, do, double, else, enum, extern, float, for, goto, if, int, long, register, return, short, signed, sizeof, static, struct, switch, typedef, union, unsigned, void, volatile, while).

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Which escape sequence character in C represents a newline?
explanation: \n inserts a line feed / newline character, moving the output cursor to the start of the next line.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What does the escape sequence '\0' signify in C programming?

options.text: The number zero as a character
The Null Character used to mark the termination of strings

explanation: \0 represents the ASCII NUL character (byte value 0x00) used universally in C as the sentinel delimiter terminating character strings.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: In C, comments that span multiple lines are enclosed between:
explanation: C multi-line block comments start with /* and end with */, whereas // begins a single-line comment introduced in C99.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What is the typical memory size occupied by a standard 'char' data type in C?
explanation: In C, sizeof(char) is defined by the standard to be guaranteed exactly 1 byte (8 bits), capable of representing 256 ASCII character values.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What is the numerical range of a signed 8-bit 'char' in two's complement representation?
explanation: An 8-bit signed integer has 2^8 = 256 states, spanning from -2^7 (-128) to +(2^7 - 1) (+127).

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: An 'unsigned char' data type in C has a value range of:
explanation: Because unsigned types carry no sign bit, all 8 bits represent magnitude, spanning from 0 to 2^8 - 1 (255).

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Which type qualifier tells the C compiler that a variable's value must not be modified by the program after initialization?
explanation: The const qualifier declares a variable read-only; attempts to assign a new value to it trigger a compiler error.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: The 'volatile' type qualifier in C indicates to the compiler optimization engine that:

options.text: The variable's memory should be cached in CPU registers permanently
The variable's value may be changed unexpectedly by hardware or external threads, preventing aggressive compiler register caching
The variable is deleted after each loop

explanation: volatile instructs the compiler to reload the variable from memory on every access because hardware memory-mapped registers or ISRs may alter it at any instant.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What is the standard precision and size difference between 'float' and 'double' in standard C?

options.text: float is 8 bytes (double precision); double is 4 bytes (single precision)
float is single precision (typically 4 bytes, ~6-7 decimal digits); double is double precision (typically 8 bytes, ~15-17 decimal digits)
Both have identical size and precision

explanation: float conforms to IEEE 754 32-bit single precision (~7 significant digits); double conforms to 64-bit double precision (~15-17 significant digits).

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Which format specifier is used in printf() to print a signed decimal integer?
explanation: %d or %i outputs signed decimal integers; %u outputs unsigned integers.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Which format specifier is used in scanf() to read a double-precision floating-point number into a variable declared as 'double'?
explanation: In scanf(), %f reads into float (4 bytes) while %lf (long float) is strictly required to read into double (8 bytes) to avoid memory corruption.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What does the format specifier '%p' display in printf()?

options.text: A pointer address in hexadecimal notation

explanation: %p is the defined conversion specifier for formatting and displaying memory address pointers (typically formatted as 0x007FFE...).

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: In C, what is the output of the expression 'sizeof(3.14)' on a standard 32/64-bit compiler?
explanation: In C, floating-point numeric literals containing a decimal point without an 'f' suffix are treated by default as 'double' literals (sizeof(double) = 8 bytes).

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What is the result of integer division '7 / 2' in C?
explanation: When both operands of the division operator (/) are integers, C performs integer truncation, discarding any fractional remainder to yield 3.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What does the modulus operator '%' calculate in C?

options.text: The integer remainder of division between two integers

explanation: The modulus operator (%) yields the remainder of integer division (e.g. 7 % 2 yields 1). Both operands must be integers.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Which of the following operations is ILLEGAL with the modulus operator (%) in C?
explanation: The modulus operator (%) in C is strictly defined for integer operands; using floating-point operands (like 10.5 % 3) generates a compilation error (use fmod() instead).

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What is the difference between prefix increment '++x' and postfix increment 'x++'?

options.text: Prefix increments after the value is used; postfix increments before
Prefix increments the variable first and returns the updated value; postfix evaluates the current value first and then increments the variable
There is no difference in C

explanation: ++x increments x immediately before expression evaluation; x++ yields the current value of x in the expression, delaying the increment until the sequence point.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: If int x = 5; what are the values of y and x after executing: int y = ++x * 2;?
explanation: Prefix ++x increments x from 5 to 6 first; then 6 * 2 = 12 is assigned to y, leaving x = 6.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: If int a = 5; what are the values of b and a after executing: int b = a++ * 2;?
explanation: Postfix a++ supplies its current value (5) for multiplication: 5 * 2 = 10 assigned to b; afterwards a is incremented to 6.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Which of the following is the Bitwise Exclusive-OR (XOR) operator in C?
explanation: In C, ^ is bitwise XOR, & is bitwise AND, | is bitwise OR, ~ is bitwise NOT (one's complement).

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What is the output of the bitwise shift expression '1 << 3' in C?
explanation: Left-shifting binary 0001 by 3 positions produces binary 1000 (decimal 8), effectively calculating 1 * 2^3.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Right-shifting a positive integer by 1 position (x >> 1) is mathematically equivalent to:
explanation: Bitwise right shift by 1 drops the least significant bit, dividing an integer by 2.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Which operator in C returns the memory footprint (in bytes) of a data type or variable at compile-time?
explanation: sizeof is a compile-time unary operator that evaluates to the number of bytes allocated for the specified type or variable.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: According to C operator precedence rules, which operator has the highest priority?
explanation: Parentheses () have the highest precedence (level 1), forcing evaluation of enclosed expressions first.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What is the value of the C expression '5 + 3 * 2'?
explanation: Multiplication has higher precedence than addition: 3 * 2 = 6, then 5 + 6 = 11.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What is the value of the expression '10 - 4 + 2' based on associativity?
explanation: Addition and subtraction share equal precedence and associate left-to-right: (10 - 4) = 6; then 6 + 2 = 8.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Which class of operators in C associates RIGHT-TO-LEFT?

options.text: Unary operators (++, --, !, sizeof) and Assignment operators (=, +=, -=)

explanation: Unary operators (++, --, !, ~) and assignment operators (=, +=) evaluate right-to-left.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What is the result of the relational expression '(5 > 3 && 2 > 8)' in C?
explanation: 5 > 3 is TRUE (1); 2 > 8 is FALSE (0); 1 && 0 evaluates to FALSE (0).

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Short-circuit evaluation in C logical AND (&&) expressions means:

options.text: If the left-hand operand evaluates to FALSE (0), the right-hand operand is completely skipped and not evaluated
Execution jumps to the end of main

explanation: In &&, if the first condition is false, the compound expression can never be true, so C aborts evaluating subsequent operands (short-circuit).

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: In C logical OR (||), short-circuit evaluation occurs when:

options.text: The left-hand operand evaluates to FALSE (0)
The left-hand operand evaluates to TRUE (non-zero)

explanation: In ||, if the left operand is TRUE, the entire statement is guaranteed to be true, so the right-hand side is bypassed.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Implicit type conversion (automatic type promotion) in C dictates that when adding an int and a float:

options.text: The float is truncated into an int
The int is promoted to a float, and floating-point addition is performed
The compiler throws a type mismatch error

explanation: C's usual arithmetic conversions promote lower-ranked types to higher-ranked types (int -> float) to avoid precision loss.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Explicit type casting from float to int in C is written as:
explanation: C uses cast notation: (type_name)expression, such as (int)3.85, which truncates the fractional part to yield 3.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What is the result of '(int)5.99 + (int)2.01' in C?
explanation: (int)5.99 truncates to 5; (int)2.01 truncates to 2; 5 + 2 = 7.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: In C, which standard header file must be included to utilize printf() and scanf()?
explanation: <stdio.h> (Standard Input Output header) contains function prototypes and definitions for streams, printf, scanf, fopen, etc.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Why is the address-of operator '&' required in 'scanf("%d", &num);'?

options.text: Because scanf requires the memory address of the variable to store the parsed input value directly into it
To calculate the percentage of num

explanation: C passes arguments by value; scanf needs the memory pointer to write the received keyboard input directly into the variable's storage cell.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Which unformatted I/O function reads a single character from standard input (stdin)?
explanation: getchar() reads and returns the next character from standard input as an unsigned char cast to an int.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Which unformatted output function displays a single character to standard output (stdout)?
explanation: putchar(char) writes a single character to the standard console display screen.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Why is the legacy function 'gets()' considered highly dangerous and deprecated in modern C standards?

options.text: It does not perform buffer bounds checking, leading to buffer overflow vulnerabilities when input exceeds array size

explanation: gets() reads until a newline without verifying array boundary capacity, allowing malicious buffer overflows (CVE security vulnerabilities).

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: Which safe string input function should replace 'gets()' to prevent buffer overflow?
explanation: fgets() mandates a maximum buffer length parameter, ensuring the input reading halts before exceeding the allocated array boundary.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What does the 'puts()' function do in addition to printing a string to the console?

options.text: Automatically appends a newline character (\n) at the end of the printed string

explanation: Unlike printf("%s", str), puts(str) automatically prints a newline character at the end of output.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: In the format specifier '%6.2f', what does the '6' and '2' specify?

options.text: 6 numbers before the decimal and 2 after
A minimum total field width of 6 characters with exactly 2 digits after the decimal point

explanation: %w.pf specifies total field width w (including sign and dot) and decimal precision p.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What is the return value of printf() upon successful execution?

options.text: The total number of characters successfully printed to output

explanation: printf() returns the total count of characters output; or a negative value if an output error occurred.

unit_title: C Fundamentals, Structure, Data Types & Operators
prompt: What does scanf() return when successfully parsing input?

options.text: The total number of input items successfully matched and assigned

explanation: scanf() returns the count of input arguments successfully scanned and assigned (e.g. scanf("%d %d", &a, &b) returns 2 on valid input).

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: Which conditional statement in C evaluates a condition and executes a block if the condition is non-zero (true)?
explanation: The 'if' statement tests a relational/logical expression; if it evaluates to any non-zero value, the nested statement block executes.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: In C, which value represents logical FALSE?
explanation: In C, 0 evaluates to FALSE, while any non-zero value (positive or negative) evaluates to TRUE.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: What is the 'Dangling Else' problem in programming languages like C?

options.text: An else statement that has no code inside it
Ambiguity in nested if-else structures where it is unclear which 'if' an 'else' belongs to without braces
An else statement placed inside a while loop
A compiler error that deletes files

explanation: In nested if statements without explicit curly braces {}, the dangling else rule resolves ambiguity by binding the 'else' to the nearest preceding unmatched 'if'.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
explanation: The condition uses assignment '=' rather than equality '=='. The expression (x = 0) assigns 0 to x and evaluates to 0 (FALSE), executing the else block to print 'B'.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: Which statement provides a multi-way branch based on comparing an integer or character expression against constant values?
explanation: The 'switch' statement evaluates an integral expression and transfers control to matching constant 'case' labels.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: What data types are strictly PERMITTED for the switch expression in standard C?
explanation: ANSI C mandates that the control expression of a switch statement and the case labels must evaluate to an integer-compatible type (int, char, enum).

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: What happens in a switch statement if a matching case is executed but does NOT end with a 'break' statement?

options.text: Execution continues sequentially into the subsequent case statements (Fall-Through)
The switch statement restarts from the beginning
The compiler throws a syntax error

explanation: Without a 'break', execution 'falls through' to execute the subsequent case and default blocks regardless of whether their labels match.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: What is the role of the 'default' label in a switch statement?

options.text: It is executed before any other case
It executes if none of the explicit case label constants match the evaluated switch expression
It is mandatory and must appear first

explanation: The optional 'default' case serves as a catch-all block executing whenever no other case constant matches the evaluated expression.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: Can a switch statement in C have two identical 'case' constant values (e.g., case 5: ... case 5:)?

options.text: No, duplicate case values cause a compilation error

explanation: The C compiler requires every case label value in a single switch block to be distinct; duplicates result in a 'duplicate case value' compile-time error.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: The conditional ternary operator in C is expressed as:
explanation: The ternary operator ? : evaluates condition; if true it yields expr1, otherwise it yields expr2.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: Which of the following is classified as an Entry-Controlled (Pre-test) loop?
explanation: A 'while' loop tests its condition before executing the loop body; if the condition is initially false, the loop body never executes (0 times).

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: Which loop guarantees that its body will execute at least ONCE regardless of the initial condition?
explanation: A 'do-while' loop is an exit-controlled (post-test) loop: the body executes first, and the test condition is evaluated at the bottom.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: In a do-while loop in C, what punctuation mark is strictly required after the while condition?
explanation: The syntax of do-while mandates a terminating semicolon after the test expression: do { ... } while (condition);

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: What are the three core expressions in a standard 'for' loop header in C?
explanation: The for loop header syntax is: for (init_expression; test_condition; update_expression).

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: What is the effect of writing 'for ( ; ; )' in C?

options.text: It causes a compilation syntax error
It creates an intentional infinite loop

explanation: Omitting all three expressions in a for loop header creates an endless loop because an omitted condition defaults to non-zero (TRUE).

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: Can a for loop initialize or update multiple variables using the comma operator?

options.text: No, only one variable is allowed in a for loop header
Yes, expressions can be separated by commas, such as for (i = 0, j = 10; i < j; i++, j--)

explanation: The comma operator allows multiple initialization and update statements within the for loop header.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: How many times does the loop 'for (int i = 1; i <= 10; i += 3)' execute?
explanation: The loop executes for i = 1, 4, 7, 10 (4 iterations). At i = 13, 13 <= 10 is false and it exits.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
explanation: The do-while loop executes the body first, printing 1 and setting x = 2. Then the condition (2 < 1) evaluates to false, terminating the loop.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: An infinite loop caused by a missing loop variable increment is an example of a:
explanation: The code compiles without syntax faults, but the program's algorithmic logic is flawed, leading to non-termination.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: What does the 'break' statement do when encountered inside a loop in C?

options.text: Skips the current iteration and jumps to the next iteration
Immediately terminates the innermost enclosing loop or switch statement and transfers control to the statement following the loop

explanation: 'break' forces immediate exit from the current innermost loop or switch-case construct.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: How does the 'continue' statement behave inside a loop?

options.text: It skips the remaining statements in the current iteration and jumps directly to the loop update/condition for the next cycle
It rewinds the loop to the beginning

explanation: 'continue' halts the active iteration, immediately bypassing subsequent statements in the loop body to start the next iteration.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: In a 'for' loop, when 'continue' is executed, control jumps directly to:

options.text: The update expression (increment/decrement), then evaluates the condition
The first statement after the loop

explanation: In a for loop, 'continue' branches directly to the update clause (e.g. i++), followed by test condition evaluation.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: In a 'while' loop, when 'continue' is executed, control jumps directly to:

options.text: The condition test expression at the top of the loop

explanation: In while and do-while loops, 'continue' jumps directly to re-evaluate the loop's test condition.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: The 'goto' statement in C performs:

options.text: An unconditional jump to a named label within the same function
A jump to an external web page

explanation: 'goto label;' unconditionally transfers program execution to 'label:', provided the target label resides in the same function scope.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: Why is the widespread use of 'goto' strongly discouraged in modern software engineering?

options.text: It creates tangled, unmaintainable 'spaghetti code' that is difficult to trace, verify, and debug
It was removed from C in 1989

explanation: Unrestricted jumps break structured single-entry single-exit flow, obscuring control flow logic.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: A label for a 'goto' statement in C is written as:
explanation: A goto label consists of a valid C identifier followed by a colon (e.g., error_cleanup:).

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: What does the 'return' statement in a C function accomplish?

options.text: It prints text on the screen
It terminates execution of the current function and optionally passes a result value back to the caller
It resets the function variables to zero

explanation: 'return' immediately exits the current function activation frame, returning execution control and any return value to the caller.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: If 'break' is used inside an inner loop of two nested loops, which loop is terminated?

options.text: Only the innermost loop containing the break statement is terminated
Only the outer loop is terminated

explanation: 'break' strictly terminates the single innermost loop level in which it resides.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: A nested loop is defined as:

options.text: A loop that contains an if statement
A loop placed completely inside the body of another loop
Two loops running on separate computers

explanation: Nested loops occur when an outer loop contains one or more inner loops, commonly used for processing multi-dimensional arrays and grids.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: If an outer loop runs 4 times and an inner loop runs 5 times for each iteration of the outer loop, how many total times does the inner loop body execute?
explanation: Total inner iterations = (outer iterations) * (inner iterations) = 4 * 5 = 20 times.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: What is the time complexity of two nested loops each iterating from 0 to N?
explanation: Each step of N outer iterations executes N inner iterations, resulting in quadratic N * N = O(N^2) computational complexity.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: In a nested loop structure, which loop completes all its iterations first?
explanation: The inner loop runs through its entire cycle from start to finish for every single incremental step of the outer loop.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt:
What does the following statement do?
while (1) { /* code */ }

options.text: Never executes because 1 is not a boolean
Executes as an intentional infinite loop until interrupted by break or return

explanation: In C, 1 represents non-zero (always TRUE), forming a standard idiom for infinite processing loops.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs

It creates an infinite loop because the while statement has an empty null body and x is never incremented
It runs normally and increments x to 5

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: Which control construct is most natural for iterating through an array of known length N?
explanation: A 'for' loop cleanly integrates counter initialization (i=0), boundary check (i<N), and step increment (i++) in a single line.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: Can a floating-point number be used as a case label in a switch statement (e.g. case 3.14:)?

options.text: Yes, any float literal is valid
No, case labels must be integral compile-time constant expressions

explanation: Floating-point literals are strictly forbidden in case labels due to binary representation inexactness.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: What is the result of evaluating: int res = (5 > 2) ? 100 : 200;
explanation: Because (5 > 2) evaluates to TRUE, the ternary operator selects and returns the first expression, 100.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: In an else-if ladder, when one condition evaluates to TRUE, what happens to subsequent else-if conditions?

options.text: All subsequent else-if and else branches are completely bypassed and skipped
The compiler executes them in parallel

explanation: An else-if chain is mutually exclusive; the first branch whose condition evaluates to TRUE executes, and control jumps to the end of the ladder.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: Can a break statement be used to exit from an 'if' statement that is NOT inside a loop or switch?

options.text: No, break is syntactically legal only within loop bodies (for, while, do) or switch blocks
Yes, if followed by a semicolon

explanation: Using 'break' outside of a loop or switch structure triggers a compile error ('break statement not within loop or switch').

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: Which of the following creates a clean menu-driven console program loop?

options.text: A do-while loop containing a switch statement

explanation: A do-while loop displays menu options, receives user input, and routes choices via a switch statement until an exit sentinel is selected.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs
prompt: Can variables be declared inside the initialization clause of a for loop (e.g., for (int i = 0; ...)) in standard ANSI C89?

options.text: No, C89 requires all variable declarations to appear at the beginning of a block; declaring inside for() was introduced in C99

explanation: In ANSI C89, loop variables had to be declared at block entry; inline loop declarations like `for (int i=0; ...)` were standardized in C99.

unit_title: Control Statements, Branching & Looping Constructs

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: An array in C is formally defined as a:

options.text: Collection of different data types stored randomly
Collection of homogeneous elements of identical data type stored in contiguous memory locations

explanation: An array stores a fixed number of elements of the same type sequentially in adjacent, contiguous memory bytes.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: In C, what is the index of the very first element of any array?
explanation: C enforces zero-based array indexing: for an array of size N, valid indices range from 0 to N-1.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: If an array is declared as 'int marks[5];', what is the index of the last valid element?
explanation: For size 5, valid indices are marks[0], marks[1], marks[2], marks[3], and marks[4].

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: What happens if a program attempts to read or write to 'arr[10]' on an array declared as 'int arr[5]' in C?

options.text: The compiler automatically resizes the array to 10
C does not perform runtime array bound checking; this accesses out-of-bounds memory causing undefined behavior or segmentation fault
The program displays a warning and pauses

explanation: C sacrifices runtime boundary checks for execution speed; out-of-bounds access corrupts adjacent memory or triggers OS segmentation faults.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: In C, what does the bare array name without subscripts (e.g. 'arr') evaluate to in most expressions?

options.text: The total sum of elements in the array
A constant pointer to the base address of the first element (&arr[0])
The number of elements in the array

explanation: An array name 'decays' into a pointer to its first element (&arr[0]) in expressions.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: Given an array 'int a[5] = {1, 2, 3};', what value is stored in 'a[3]'?
explanation: When an array initializer list provides fewer elements than declared capacity, C automatically initializes all remaining elements to zero (0).

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: What is stored in elements of a local (automatic) array if NO initialization list is provided?
explanation: Local automatic variables and arrays allocated on the stack are not automatically cleared; their contents remain random garbage bytes.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: How do you calculate the number of elements in an array 'int arr[] = {10, 20, 30, 40, 50};' using sizeof?
explanation: Total array size in bytes divided by the size of one element yields the exact element count (e.g. 20 bytes / 4 bytes = 5 elements).

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: Given base address 1000 and 4-byte integers, what is the memory address of element arr[3]?
explanation: Address formula: Base + (index * sizeof(type)) = 1000 + (3 * 4) = 1000 + 12 = 1012.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: Can an array in standard C be resized dynamically after its fixed declaration without using DMA?

options.text: No, standard C arrays have fixed, immutable memory bounds allocated at declaration
Yes, by assigning a new size to the array name

explanation: Fixed array sizes are determined at compile/allocation time; resizing requires dynamic memory functions like realloc().

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: A two-dimensional array 'int matrix[3][4];' contains how many total integer elements?
explanation: Total elements = rows * columns = 3 * 4 = 12 elements.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: In C memory architecture, multi-dimensional arrays are stored in which order?
explanation: C stores 2D arrays in Row-Major order: all elements of row 0 are placed sequentially, followed immediately by row 1, row 2, etc.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: For an array 'int A[R][C]' with base address B and element size S, the address of element A[i][j] in Row-Major order is:
explanation: Row-major address formula: Base + ((row_index * TOTAL_COLUMNS) + col_index) * element_size.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: How do you declare and initialize a 2x2 identity matrix in C?

options.text: Both A and B are valid initializations

explanation: Both flat initialization {1, 0, 0, 1} and nested row initialization {{1, 0}, {0, 1}} are valid C syntax.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: What condition must be satisfied to perform Matrix Multiplication between matrix A of size (M x N) and matrix B of size (P x Q)?

options.text: N must equal P (columns of A must equal rows of B)

explanation: Matrix multiplication A x B is valid only when the number of columns in matrix A matches the number of rows in matrix B.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: The transpose of a matrix is obtained by:

options.text: Inverting every sign of the numbers
Interchanging rows into columns and columns into rows

explanation: Transpose swaps indices: element A[i][j] moves to position A_transposed[j][i].

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: In a square matrix of size N x N, an element A[i][j] lies on the Main Diagonal when:
explanation: The main diagonal contains elements where row index equals column index (A[0][0], A[1][1], ..., A[N-1][N-1]).

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: A matrix that has non-zero elements only on its main diagonal, with all other elements equal to zero, is a:
explanation: A diagonal matrix has non-zero values strictly where i == j, and zero everywhere else.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: A matrix where the vast majority of its elements are zero is termed a:
explanation: A sparse matrix contains relatively few non-zero entries, often represented efficiently using coordinate triples to save RAM.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: When passing a 2D array to a C function, which dimension is MANDATORY in the function parameter declaration?

options.text: The first dimension (row count) must be specified
The second dimension (column count) must be specified (e.g. void f(int arr[][4]))

explanation: The C compiler needs the column width to calculate row address offsets (i * COLS); hence the column size cannot be omitted.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: In C, a string is conventionally represented as a:

options.text: One-dimensional array of characters terminated by a null character ('\0')

explanation: C has no native 'string' primitive type; strings are arrays of char ending with the sentinel null byte '\0'.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: How many bytes of memory are allocated for the string literal "Rohilkhand"?
explanation: "Rohilkhand" contains 10 alphabetical characters plus 1 mandatory terminating '\0' byte = 11 bytes total.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: What is the difference between single quotes 'A' and double quotes "A" in C?

options.text: 'A' is a single character constant (ASCII 65); "A" is a string literal array containing 'A' and '\0'
'A' is a string; "A" is a char

explanation: 'A' evaluates to an integer ASCII value (65); "A" represents a 2-byte null-terminated string array in memory.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: What happens when reading a string using 'scanf("%s", str);' if the user enters 'MJP Rohilkhand'?

options.text: It reads the entire line 'MJP Rohilkhand'
It reads only 'MJP' because %s stops reading at the first whitespace character

explanation: %s in scanf() treats space, tab, and newline as delimiters, halting input capture at the first whitespace.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: Which standard input function correctly reads an entire line of text including spaces until a newline is pressed?
explanation: fgets() reads characters including spaces until a newline is encountered or the specified buffer limit is reached.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: What does the 'strlen()' function in <string.h> return?

options.text: The total memory allocated for the character array
The number of characters in the string, excluding the terminating null character ('\0')

explanation: strlen() counts characters sequentially starting from the base address until it encounters '\0', excluding '\0' from the tally.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: Which function from <string.h> is used to copy the contents of source string 'src' into destination buffer 'dest'?
explanation: strcpy(dest, src) copies characters from src into dest including the terminating '\0'.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: The 'strcat(str1, str2)' function performs:

options.text: String concatenation (appends a copy of str2 to the end of str1)

explanation: strcat() appends the second string to the first string, overwriting the original '\0' of str1 and appending a new '\0' at the end.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: What does 'strcmp(str1, str2)' return when both strings are identical?
explanation: strcmp() performs lexicographical comparison: it returns 0 if strings match identically, negative if str1 < str2, positive if str1 > str2.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: What is the result of 'strcmp("apple", "banana")'?
explanation: At the first character, 'a' (ASCII 97) minus 'b' (ASCII 98) = -1 (negative), indicating 'apple' precedes 'banana'.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: Which function searches for the first occurrence of a specific character in a string?
explanation: strchr(str, ch) locates the first instance of character ch in str and returns a pointer to it (or NULL if not found).

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: Which function searches for the first occurrence of a substring within another string?
explanation: strstr(haystack, needle) searches for the first occurrence of substring 'needle' within 'haystack'.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: What is the safe alternative to strcpy() that limits the number of copied characters to prevent buffer overflow?
explanation: strncpy() copies at most n characters, shielding the destination array from unbounded overflow.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: How would you write a custom function to calculate string length without using strlen()?

options.text: Iterate a pointer or index while (str[i] != '\0') incrementing a counter

explanation: A simple while (str[len] != '\0') len++; loop counts characters up to the null byte.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: When comparing two strings for case-insensitive equality in POSIX / non-standard C libraries, which function is used?
explanation: strcasecmp() (or strcmpi/stricmp) compares strings ignoring uppercase/lowercase distinctions.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: What does the non-standard function 'strrev(str)' do?

options.text: Reverses the order of characters in the string in-place
Returns the length of the string

explanation: strrev() reverses characters within the string buffer (e.g. "cat" becomes "tac").

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: Which function converts all uppercase letters in a string to lowercase?
explanation: strlwr() converts ASCII uppercase letters in a string to lowercase.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: If char s[] = "Hello"; what is sizeof(s) and strlen(s)?
explanation: sizeof(s) includes the trailing '\0' byte (6 bytes total); strlen(s) counts only the 5 visible letters.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: Can you assign a new string to an already declared array using the assignment operator (e.g., char s[20]; s = "Hello";)?

options.text: Yes, that is standard C syntax
No, array names are constant pointers and cannot be l-values on the left of assignment; use strcpy() instead
Yes, if the string is under 20 chars

explanation: Arrays cannot be assigned to directly after definition because array identifiers are non-modifiable lvalues; strcpy() must be used.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: In C, an array declared as 'static int numbers[5];' initializes its elements to:
explanation: Static and global storage class variables and arrays are automatically zero-initialized by the compiler/runtime.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: What does the expression '*(arr + i)' represent?

options.text: The memory address of element i
The value of array element arr[i]
The multiplication of arr and i

explanation: In C, array subscript notation arr[i] is defined as syntactical sugar for pointer dereference *(arr + i).

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: Is the expression 'i[arr]' valid syntax in C programming?

options.text: No, it causes a severe syntax error
Yes, because *(arr + i) and *(i + arr) are mathematically identical in pointer addition

explanation: Because addition is commutative, *(arr + i) == *(i + arr), which allows the unconventional but valid syntax i[arr].

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: To store a list of 10 student names where each name can be up to 50 characters long, you declare a:
explanation: A 2D character array char names[10][50] provides 10 rows (strings), each holding up to 50 characters (including '\0').

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: What is an array of pointers in C?

options.text: A pointer pointing to an array
An array whose elements are memory address pointers pointing to other data items

explanation: An array of pointers (e.g. int *ptrs[5]) contains multiple pointer variables as its elements.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt:
In C, what is the effect of passing an array to a function?
void modify(int a[]) { a[0] = 99; }

options.text: The function receives a copy; the caller's array remains unchanged
The array decays into a pointer; changes made to elements inside the function directly modify the caller's original array
The compiler throws a type error

explanation: Arrays are passed by reference (as pointers to their base address); modifications within the function alter the original caller elements.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: Which searching algorithm checks each array element sequentially from the first to the last until the target key is found?
explanation: Linear Search scans elements sequentially one by one in O(N) time without requiring sorted data.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: Binary Search requires that the input array must strictly be:

options.text: Sorted in ascending or descending order

explanation: Binary Search requires a sorted array to divide the search space in half each step in O(log N) time.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: What is the worst-case time complexity of Bubble Sort on an array of size N?
explanation: Bubble Sort compares adjacent pairs in nested passes, requiring approximately N*(N-1)/2 comparisons = O(N^2) worst-case time.

unit_title: Arrays, 2D Arrays, Strings & String Handling Functions
prompt: The process of combining two previously sorted arrays into a single sorted array is called:
explanation: Merging takes two sorted lists and combines them in linear O(N + M) time into a unified sorted sequence (foundation of Merge Sort).

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: What is the primary motivation for using functions in C programming?

options.text: To make the program file larger
Modular programming, code reusability, easier debugging, and reduction of redundant code

explanation: Functions decompose complex software into self-contained logical modules, promoting clean architecture and reusable subroutines.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: A Function Declaration (Function Prototype) tells the C compiler:

options.text: The exact assembly instructions of the function
The function name, return type, and the number and types of its parameters before its definition
The variable values inside the function
The hard disk sector where code lives

explanation: Prototypes inform the compiler of a function's signature so calls can be type-checked before the full definition is parsed.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: Which of the following represents a valid function prototype in C?
explanation: A function prototype specifies the return type, identifier, parameter types in parentheses, and ends with a semicolon: int sum(int, int);

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: If a function does NOT return any value to the caller, its return type must be declared as:
explanation: The 'void' keyword indicates the absence of a return value.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: In C, arguments passed into a function call are called:
explanation: Actual arguments are the real values or variables supplied during a function call: e.g. in add(x, y), x and y are actual arguments.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: The parameter variables declared in the function header definition that receive incoming values are called:
explanation: Formal parameters are placeholders defined in the function signature that receive copied values when called.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: What is the default return type of a C function if no return type is explicitly specified (in traditional C89)?
explanation: Classic C assumed 'implicit int' return type if omitted, though modern C99/C11 standards deprecate this practice.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: Can a C function return multiple values directly through a standard return statement?

options.text: No, a C function can return at most one single value via return; returning multiple values requires pointers or structures

explanation: The return statement transfers exactly one value; returning multiple results requires passing pointers (simulating reference) or returning a struct.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: What happens when execution encounters a 'return;' statement inside a void function?

options.text: Execution terminates immediately and control returns to the caller

explanation: In void functions, a bare 'return;' immediately exits the function frame and returns control to the caller.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: Can one function definition be nested directly inside the body of another function definition in standard ANSI C?

options.text: Yes, nested functions are standard in C
No, standard C does not support nested function definitions; all functions must be defined at file scope
Only if the inner function is void

explanation: ANSI C requires all function definitions to reside at the global/file scope level; nesting function bodies inside other functions is illegal in standard C.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: By default, all primitive scalar arguments in C are passed to functions by:
explanation: C evaluates all scalar parameters using Call by Value: the function receives independent copies of the caller's values.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: In Call by Value, modifications made to formal parameters inside the called function:

options.text: Permanently alter the caller's original actual variables
Have absolutely no effect on the caller's original actual variables

explanation: Because formal parameters are distinct local copies stored in a separate stack frame, modifying them does not alter the caller's data.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: How does a C programmer achieve 'Call by Reference' behavior to allow a function to modify caller variables?

options.text: By passing the memory addresses of variables (&var) and receiving them as pointers (*ptr)

explanation: C simulates pass-by-reference by passing pointers (addresses) to variables, allowing the function to dereference and modify caller memory directly.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: Which function signature correctly swaps two integer variables using simulated call by reference in C?
explanation: void swap(int *a, int *b) receives pointers to the caller's variables and swaps their contents via dereferencing (*a and *b).

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: Inside the function 'void swap(int *a, int *b)', the swapping logic is written as:

options.text: temp = a; a = b; b = temp;

explanation: Dereferencing (*a, *b) accesses and updates the actual integer values stored at the caller's memory locations.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: When an array is passed to a function (e.g. printArray(arr, 5);), how is it passed?

options.text: A complete deep copy of all array elements is pushed to stack
The array decays into a pointer to its first element (simulated call by reference)
Only the first element is passed by value
Arrays cannot be passed to functions

explanation: Passing an array passes its base memory address; changes to array elements within the function directly alter the original array.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: Why is passing large data structures via pointers more efficient than passing them by value?

options.text: Passing a pointer copies only a tiny address (4 or 8 bytes) rather than copying the entire large memory block onto the call stack

explanation: Passing by address avoids high stack overhead and CPU copy cycles associated with duplicating large structures in memory.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
prompt: What does the 'const' qualifier indicate when applied to a pointer parameter: 'void print(const int *p)'?

options.text: The pointer itself cannot point anywhere else
The function promises NOT to modify the integer value pointed to by p

explanation: const int *p enforces read-only access to the caller's data, triggering a compiler error if the function attempts to modify *p.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
explanation: Because C uses Call by Value, test() modifies its local copy x; the caller's variable 'a' remains 5.

unit_title: Functions, Parameter Passing, Recursion & Scope
